domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
t is real and satisfies 1 - 1/n <= t < 1
k is an integer satisfying 1 <= k <= n
floor is the standard floor function on real inputs
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n>1 and every real t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1, for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n we have floor(k*t) = k - 1; therefore (by the definition of f_n and H_n used in the surrounding context) f_n(t) equals H_n - 1 for all such t.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n>1
for all real t with 1 - 1/n <= t and t < 1
for all integers k with 1 <= k and k <= n

variables.name: n
variables.role: main index; upper bound for k and denominator in the bound for t

variables.name: t
variables.role: parameter constrained by an interval depending on n

variables.name: k
variables.role: quantified index for the floor expression; range tied to n

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses: all quantified variables are universal.
The final consequence f_n(t) = H_n - 1 is intended to depend on the fact that floor(k*t) equals k - 1 for all integers k in 1..n.

statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n; consequently, f_n(t) = H_n - 1.
